version.note: The performing edition and any editorial alterations are not identified in the recording sources.

date.note: Young lists CVE-48987-1 with the recording date 24 April 1929, DAHR lists CVE-48987 among the Boston Symphony Orchestra and Koussevitzky recordings of Symphony No. 94 made that day, and the Bolig discography assigns the Menuetto to that matrix. Commons’ 1 January 1929 is not a session day.

place.value: Symphony Hall, Boston, Massachusetts, United States
place.note: Young heads the 22 April 1929 session “Symphony Hall, Boston, Massachusetts” and lists the 24 April retaken sides of the same symphony under that session; DAHR gives Symphony Hall, Boston for the Andante side CVE-48984. A separate place for the 24 April retakes is not given.

catalogue.note: Young lists the symphony as released 9/29 on M-55 (7058/60), with later AM-55, DM-55, HMV and LP issues. The upstream transfer also names set M-55 (Internet Archive description), and DAHR places the Andante on disc 7059. The disc number of this movement’s sides is not stated; the side order (sides 1–2 movement I, sides 3–4 the Andante, sides 5–6 the Menuetto and Finale) suggests 7058 for movement I and 7060 for the Menuetto and Finale, but that allocation is inferred.

matrixTakeSides.note: Young and Bolig agree on the matrix and take (one take issued of four made, per Young’s bracketed count). The DAHR matrix page could not be opened on 17 October 2026 (503 error). No run-out inspection has been made of the digital surrogate.

credits.value: Bob Varney — transfer from original Victor 78s

date.note: No transfer date is identified. The Internet Archive item was uploaded in December 2008, which is an upload date.

processing.value: Transfer from the original Victor 78 rpm set M-55 into one 20:48 file, from which the four movements were extracted as separate Commons files.
processing.note: The file lengths of the four Commons movements sum to the length of the Internet Archive file within about a second. The extraction procedure, stylus, playback curve, side-join locations and noise treatment are not documented.

digital.format: MP3 access derivative supplied by Wikimedia Commons; uploaded source: Ogg Vorbis

composition.value: Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies.
composition.note: Haydn died in 1809. This is a term calculation, not a worldwide clearance or a statement about an unidentified modern edition.

recording.value: Rule 3 — territorial: sound recording public domain in the European Union (pre-1963 publication basis).
recording.note: Commons applies PD-EU-audio to the Koussevitzky/Boston recording attributed to 1929, and the Internet Archive item carries a Creative Commons public-domain licence URL, not treated here as authority to waive Victor’s rights. The programme’s pre-1963 European rule applies because the 50-year term had expired before the 2013 extension; Young gives the release as September 1929, which supports first publication well before 1963. This is territorial, not a worldwide licence; US status is not established.

alternatives.value: PD-EU-audio — European performers’ and producers’ rights claimed expired.
